chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from a number of our companions, from a man from the people of Khurasan that a question arose during

the pilgrimage season, and there was no prohibited item with his freed slaves regarding it, so he pulled out a tooth, and the Imam (peace be upon him) wrote on it: 'It sheds blood.' And there is no harm if the meat of game is with the one in ihram, provided he does not eat it and keeps it until the time of his tahallul, if he himself hunted it.

key_terms.إِحْلاَلِهِ: his exit from ihram (completion of rituals)
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: one in the state of ihram (ritual consecration)
key_terms.يُهَرِيقُ دَماً: it sheds blood (legal term for blood-money penalty)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on possessing hunted meat while in ihram if you didn't hunt it yourself?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the distinction between active hunting and mere possession in the state of ihram, ruling that keeping hunted meat is permissible if the pilgrim did not personally hunt it, thereby avoiding the penalty of 'shedding blood' (diya) associated with pulling out a tooth. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the specific conditions of the hunter's agency when determining liability for violations of ihram restrictions.
